title: The Search for Solid Ground in Text as Data: A Systematic Review of Validation Practices and Practical Recommendations for Validation
citation: Birkenmaier, L., Lechner, C. M., & Wagner, C. (2024). The search for solid ground in text as data: A systematic review of validation practices and practical recommendations for validation. Communication Methods and Measures, 18(3), 249–277. https://doi.org/10.1080/19312458.2023.2285765
relation: directly addresses construct validation practices in computational communication; our novelty is post-classification object ranking, not validation generally.

title: Misclassification in Automated Content Analysis Causes Bias in Regression. Can We Fix It? Yes We Can!
citation: TeBlunthuis, N., Hase, V., & Chan, C.-H. (2024). Misclassification in automated content analysis causes bias in regression. Can we fix it? Yes we can! Communication Methods and Measures, 18(3), 278–299. https://doi.org/10.1080/19312458.2023.2293713
relation: direct competitor in downstream error correction; their focal issue is regression bias, whereas the present paper audits pairwise descriptive rank reversals and human-label budgets.

title: Enhancing Data Quality through Simple De-duplication: Navigating Responsible Computational Social Science Research
citation: Mu, Y., Jin, M., Song, X., & Aletras, N. (2024). Enhancing data quality through simple de-duplication: Navigating responsible computational social science research. In Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (pp. 12477–12492). Association for Computational Linguistics. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.emnlp-main.694
relation: direct relevance to deduplication and leakage; this paper treats unique text versus repeated records as alternative estimands, not unilaterally improved accuracy.

title: Natural language processing for social science research: A comprehensive review
citation: Hou, Y., & Huang, J. (2025). Natural language processing for social science research: A comprehensive review. Chinese Journal of Sociology, 11(1). https://doi.org/10.1177/2057150X241306780
relation: background review on representativeness, interpretability and bias; broad context not direct prior rank-reversal study.

title: Critical, but constructive: defining, detecting, and addressing bias in Computational Social Science
citation: Hase, V., Bachl, M., & TeBlunthuis, N. (2025). Critical, but constructive: Defining, detecting, and addressing bias in computational social science. Communication Methods and Measures, 19(4), 281–293. https://doi.org/10.1080/19312458.2025.2575468
relation: framework context on defining/detecting/addressing bias; supports method-level contribution but no claim of novelty of bias correction.
